rules.title: Application screening fee cap ($30 adjusted for CPI)
rules.requirement: A landlord may charge an application screening fee no greater than its actual out-of-pocket screening costs, and never more than $30 per applicant, adjusted annually for CPI since 1998. The landlord must give an itemized receipt, refund any unused part of the fee, and give you a copy of your credit report within 7 days of receiving it.
rules.coverage_conditions: Owners of residential rental property and their agents who charge applicants, including guarantors and cosigners, a nonrefundable fee to screen an application.
rules.exemptions: Does not preempt rules on deposits and fees under federal or state housing assistance programs.
rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant.

rules.title: Limits on when a screening fee may be charged; first-come process or refund
rules.requirement: A landlord may not charge a screening fee if it knows or should know that no unit is or soon will be available. It may charge one only if it either considers applications in the order received and approves the first qualified applicant, or refunds the whole fee to every applicant not selected within 7 days of selecting a tenant or 30 days after the application, whichever comes first.
rules.key_value: Refund within 7 days of selection or 30 days of application, whichever is first (if the first-come process is not used)
rules.coverage_conditions: Owners of residential rental property and their agents who charge application screening fees.
rules.exemptions: No refund is required under the first-come process for an applicant who is denied after consideration for failing the landlord's written screening criteria.

notes: Secondary mirror (california.public.law) of Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6, which it says was updated Jan. 1, 2026. The document gives no enactment date or amendment date, so effective_date is left null. The rule appears to be in force based on the mirror's update note. The only date in the text is that CPI adjustment of the $30 cap starts on 1998-01-01. The subdivision (c)(2) process and refund requirements came from a later amendment whose date the document does not give. The section has no penalty provision. Subdivision (g), on reusable screening reports under § 1950.1, is mentioned but not extracted as a separate rule.
